subject: Re: Competitive evaluation — model quality follow-ups and next tests
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>

Subject: Post-call recap and proposed next tests

Hi Ava & Samir,

Thanks again for taking the time today — great conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned:  

Summary from our discovery call:  
- Primary use case: real-time transaction categorization + customer-facing explainability.
- Key constraints: P95 latency < 150ms for single-turn classification, strict PII handling, SOC2 requirements, and enterprise procurement timeline (~8 weeks).
- Current integration: prototype calling HyperscalerAPI via their hosted endpoints; concerns about hallucination on long-context prompts and token costs at scale.

What we propose as next steps (agreement = run short eval suite):
1) Redwood runs a head-to-head model-quality comparison (your eval prompts) against their current HyperscalerAPI baseline. We'll measure accuracy, hallucination rate on our hallucination set, and latency/throughput on your representative payloads.
2) We will provide a short report with sample outputs, hallucination examples, and a recommended configuration (batching/quantization/pinned models) to hit your cost/latency targets.
3) Schedule 30-min review on the week of Nov 23 to walk the results + ops considerations.

What we need from you to run the initial tests:  
- The CSV with the eval prompts and labels (a few hundred rows is ideal).
- A sample of typical payloads (size distribution, avg tokens).
- Any priority edge-case prompt types (legal/regulatory language, truncated context).

I attached a short test plan and example comparison matrix (redwood_vs_hyperscaler_comparison.pdf). If you can share the eval CSV we'll queue the tests for next week.

Thanks — happy to adjust scope based on what you prefer.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0172

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: FW: Post-call recap and proposed next tests — FintechCo eval (results and next steps)

Marissa / Ava — quick update; initial run completed and attached is the short summary. Highlights:  

- Dataset: received fintechco_eval_prompts.csv (450 labeled rows) + 40 hallucination challenge prompts.
- Accuracy: Redwood (recommended policy: redwood-3b-q4f) achieved 87.3% top-1 accuracy vs labeled intents; HyperscalerAPI baseline returned 82.1% on the same set.
- Hallucination rate (challenge set): Redwood flagged 4/40 clear hallucinations (10%), HyperscalerAPI flagged 9/40 (22%). Examples of hallucination differences included regulatory citations invented by baseline on legal-sounding prompts — attached excerpts in the PDF.
- Latency: single-shot median P50 = 62ms, P95 = 138ms (measured on a dedicated small pool); HyperscalerAPI P95 ~ 210ms on their hosted endpoint for same payloads. Batched throughput (batch=16) for Redwood: ~420 reqs/s; batch=32: ~560 reqs/s (we included a short screencap).
- Cost estimate: token cost delta in favor of Redwood when configured with batching and KV prefix caching; see summary table in PDF.

Next steps we recommend:
1) Run a small regulatory-safety focused eval (50 prompts) where we instrument hallucination confidence thresholds and response redaction settings. Could run as a 1-hour live session with the FintechCo team to walk examples.
2) If results look good, we propose a short POC: 2-week dedicated pool with config we validated (pinned model + caching + autoscale limits) to simulate production load.

Attachments: redwood_vs_hyperscaler_comparison.pdf, fintechco_eval_outputs.zip (raw outputs), screencap-throughput.mp4

Rishi Malhotra
Principal Applied ML Engineer, Redwood Inference
